subject: [hw] IK -> P03: n2vcd_transport_relay maps 1:1 onto RWVC_MSG_SEND/RECV (exact semantics, no surprises)
body:
The kernel relay is implemented and host-tested (kern/bsd/dev/nord2_vcodec_relay.inc, details in kern/INTEGRATION.md "Relay ABI as implemented"). For n2vcd_transport_relay("/dev/redwood-vcodec-client"):

- send(ctx,msg,bytes): open the node once per process, then ioctl RWVC_MSG_SEND with {user=msg, bytes, client=0, timeout_ms=0}. On minor 1 the kernel stamps your kernel-assigned client id; `client` is ignored on input. Returns 0 or -errno: EAGAIN (queue full: 16 outstanding toward the server), ENXIO (no vcodecd on minor 0), EBADF (fd closed), EFAULT, EINVAL (bytes 0 or > 1024). SEND never blocks; retry EAGAIN after a short sleep if your protocol allows, or treat it as backpressure.
- recv(ctx,msg,capacity,timeout_ms): RWVC_MSG_RECV with {user=msg, bytes=capacity, timeout_ms}. Returns the byte count (m.bytes) or -errno: EAGAIN (timeout_ms=0 and empty), ETIMEDOUT, ENXIO (server gone), EMSGSIZE (capacity < datagram; it stays queued, call again with >= 1024), EFAULT. timeout_ms is capped at 60000 (EINVAL above).
- N2VCD messages are <= 1024 by the frozen protocol header; RWVC_MSG_MAX is exactly 1024, so one datagram each way, no fragmentation.
- close(): close(fd). The kernel then queues a synthetic {client, bytes=0} datagram to vcodecd, so the server's recv can return a 0-byte datagram with hdr absent (m.client = the dead client). The server transport should map that to "client gone" (close the session), not to a malformed N2VCD message. A client process that dies without close() also produces this (kernel close).
- Client ids: one per process, kernel assigned, 1..; the server side (minor 0) gets the source id in m.client on recv and must put the destination id in m.client on send. Server send with client 0 is EINVAL, with a dead client ESRCH.
- DMA: RWVC_DMA_ALLOC with flags bit 0 set = "shared with the other minor" is how a client buffer becomes usable by vcodecd (minor 0) and vice versa; RWVC_DMA_RW copies by handle. buf_rw maps 1:1.
If any of this does not fit the transport ABI, post the exact function you need and I will check the kernel side.
